questions.stem: A 70-year-old man with early dementia refuses surgery. His son wants him declared incompetent. Who makes that determination?

options.A: The treating physician, through a capacity assessment
options.B: A psychiatrist, since dementia is a mental disorder
options.C: A judge, possibly after consulting physicians
options.E: The son, as next of kin

questions.explanation: Competence is a legal term, and only the judge determines it; physicians are often consulted about the patient's decision-making capacity. If found incompetent, the court appoints a legal guardian. A, B: Physicians assess capacity, a clinical term, not legal competence. D: Not the body that rules on competence. E: Relatives cannot declare competence; all adults are presumed competent.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old married woman who cares for her 1-year-old son comes alone to the clinic and requests treatment for herself. Her parents live in another city. Who can consent to her treatment?

options.A: Her parents, since she is younger than 18
options.B: Her husband, as her legal representative
options.D: No one; treatment must wait until she turns 18
options.E: She can consent herself as an emancipated minor

questions.explanation: Minors (<18) are not legally competent, but an emancipated minor (self-supporting or in the military, or married or caring for her own children) is considered an adult and consents to her own care. A: Parental consent is not needed once emancipated. B: Marriage makes her emancipated; it does not transfer decisions to her husband. C: Guardians are appointed for persons found incompetent. D: She can consent now.

questions.stem: While examining a 25-year-old woman, a Lebanese physician finds evidence that she was raped. According to Article 7 (professional secrecy) of the Lebanese code, what must the physician do?

options.A: Report to the appropriate authorities whatever the victim wishes
options.B: Report to the Public Prosecutor if the victim gives written consent
options.C: Notify the Ministry of Public Health
options.D: Keep it secret unless summoned by the court as an expert
options.E: Report only if the physician believes it will prevent further crimes

questions.explanation: Article 7, clause 13: cases of rape and offenses against honor are reported to the Public Prosecutor provided the victim gives written consent. A: Reporting without consent applies to minors or incapacitated persons (clause 14). C: Notification to the Ministry is for reportable venereal diseases (clause 9). D: The expert exemption (clause 7) is a different situation. E: That wording concerns crimes the physician discovers, not this clause.

questions.stem: During a routine visit, an adult patient confesses to his Lebanese physician that he committed a burglary last year. According to Article 7 of the Lebanese code, what should the physician do?

options.B: Report it to the public prosecution
options.C: Report it to the judicial police
options.D: Report it only if the patient gives written consent
options.E: Warn the victim directly, as in the Tarasoff decision

questions.explanation: Article 7, clause 5: a physician shall not report a crime that a patient confessed to; only a crime the physician discovers during examination must be reported to the public prosecution. B: Applies to crimes discovered on examination, not confessed ones. C: Even when summoned by the judicial police, the physician may keep some secrets (clause 4). D: Written consent is the condition for reporting rape (clause 13). E: Tarasoff concerns a credible threat to another person, not a past crime.

questions.stem: In a Lebanese hospital, a competent 40-year-old man whose beliefs forbid blood transfusion refuses blood. He then develops hemorrhage that puts his life in permanent danger. According to the Lebanese code, what should the physician do?

options.B: Respect the refusal in all circumstances
options.C: Obtain consent for transfusion from his family
options.D: Obtain judicial authorization, then act by professional conscience
options.E: Advise him of his responsibility and report to the health authorities

questions.explanation: Clause 9: the physician respects the refusal, except when there is permanent danger; then, after obtaining authorization from the appropriate judicial authorities, the physician acts according to professional conscience, bearing full responsibility. A: Judicial authorization is required first. B: The law makes an exception for permanent danger. C: Family consent is not the mechanism in the law. E: That is the rule for refusal of required vaccinations (clause 8).

questions.stem: One month after naming her neighbor in a durable power of attorney for health care, a 75-year-old woman has a stroke and is unlikely to regain consciousness. Her son, who lives with her, insists on continued life support; the neighbor asks that it be withdrawn. Whose decision should the physician follow?

options.A: The son's, as next of kin
options.B: The neighbor's, as her designated representative
options.C: The physician's own judgment of her best interest
options.E: Neither; keep her on life support until they agree

questions.explanation: A durable power of attorney is an advance directive in which a competent person designates someone as her legal representative for health care decisions when she can no longer make them, so the neighbor decides. A: Family members act as surrogates (substituted judgment) only when there is no advance directive, and their personal wishes are irrelevant. C: Best-interest decisions apply when no surrogate is available. D: A valid designated representative already exists. E: The designated representative's decision stands.
